extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, engineers, and educators (readers/contributors to the Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for constructing a Universal Alphabet and a teaching primer: rules for what counts as a single sound, how to assign characters, notation and accenting, and a stepwise method for teaching reading and spelling. (The page also contains technical rules for hydraulics and empirical tests for identifying stones.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow through bores proportional to square of diameter
rubrics_metrics.description: The quantity evacuated by different bores, at the same height of the reservoir, are as the squares of the diameters of the bores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as a general experimental rule in the discourse on measuring running and spouting waters (third part, third discourse). It is used to compute comparative discharge for pipes of differing bores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow versus reservoir height (subduple proportion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The quantity of water expended by a jet d'eau, of the same diameter of bore, but at different heights of the reservoir, are in a subduple proportion of these heights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an experimental finding (third part, second discourse). Use this relation when predicting changes in discharge from change of head for identical bores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jets never reach reservoir height (duplicate proportion shortfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jets d'eau never rise so high as their reservoirs, but always fall short, by spaces which are in duplicate proportion of the heights they rise to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by experiments (fourth part, first discourse). This quantifies expected fall-short of jet height relative to reservoir and should inform design/expectation of fountain performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ajutage (nozzle) shape affects jet height
rubrics_metrics.description: An even polished round hole in the end of the pipe gives a higher jet than either a cylindric or conical ajutage; of these latter the conical is the better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental recommendation for best sort of spouts for jets d'eau (fourth part). Use polished round openings when maximum jet height is desired; conical preferred over cylindrical if round not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipe sizing rule (squares of diameters)
rubrics_metrics.description: The squares of the diameters of the pipes be as the quantity of water to be expended; when a great pipe branches into several smaller distributed to different jets, the square of the diameter of the main pipe must be proportioned to the sum of all the expenses of its branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given as a rule to avoid increased friction and unequal running speeds in small pipes (fifth part, first discourse). Use this proportionality when selecting pipe diameters to maintain uniform velocity and frictional conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipe strength must bear water pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipes must have requisite strength for bearing the pressure of the water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed with reference to experiments on resistance of solids (fifth part, second discourse). Design pipe wall thickness/materials based on expected internal pressures as evidenced by experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipe cleansing and air removal via apertures
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipes are to be cleansed from mud by leaving apertures to let out the water in those places where the pipes lie lowest; and from air by like apertures left on the tops of those eminences where the pipes pass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical distribution/maintenance recommendation (fifth part, last discourse). Include low-point drains and high-point air vents in piping layouts to allow flushing and degassing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for floating bodies and equilibrium of fluids
rubrics_metrics.description: From the principles of mechanics, fluids counterpoise each other's weight and give rules for the doctrine of floating bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in the second part (first discourse) as mechanics-derived principles governing buoyancy and equilibrium; use these mechanical principles when assessing flotation and counterpoise in fluid bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipollence of a fluid to a stroke and rules for jets
rubrics_metrics.description: A fluid body has equipollence to a stroke or shock; rules are given for the force of jets d'eau from several heights of the reservoir and different diameters of the bore of the pipe; comparative force of wind and water-mills and manner of computing them is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are presented as theory and computational guidance (second part, third discourse). Apply these rules when computing jet forces and comparing wind vs water mill power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabet must enumerate all single sounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A Universal Alphabet should contain an enumeration of all such single sounds, or letters, as are used in any language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivated by difficulties in writing/pronouncing languages with existing alphabets; the alphabet's purpose is to enable true, unambiguous pronunciation and description of any language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique mapping: one character per sound and vice versa
rubrics_metrics.description: No one character should have more than one sound, nor any one sound be expressed by more than one character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as a benefit/requirement of the Universal Alphabet: ensures that false pronunciation will be easily discovered because it would correspond to another character's true sound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1 — single sounds not describable as conjunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: That no true single sound can be justly described or expressed by the conjunction of any two or more other single sounds (i.e. a vowel not by other vowels, a consonant not by other consonants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of three fundamental rules for defining single sounds (Lodwick). Use this as a test when determining whether a sound is atomic or composite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 2 — inability to express a sound by conjunction => compounded
rubrics_metrics.description: That whatever sound cannot be expressed or described, except by the conjunction of two or more single sounds, it is no single but a compounded sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines compounded sounds operationally: if only reproducible as a sequence of other single sounds, treat it as compound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3 — constituent single sounds must be discernible in compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: That in every composition of single sounds, the particular single sounds which make up that composition ought to be truly and clearly discerned in the sound of the composition; otherwise it cannot truly be said to be a composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audibility of components as a criterion to decide whether a purported compound is truly composed of its claimed single sounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction and definitions of vowels and consonants
rubrics_metrics.description: Vowels are such as are singly expressible (e, a, o, &c.); consonants are such as cannot singly be expressed without the conjunction of a vowel (b, d, f, g, &c.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic phonetic classification for constructing the Universal Alphabet and primers; underlies placement and combination rules in the proposed script.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for long and short vowel sounds
rubrics_metrics.description: These vowels have each a long and a short sound (short as in 'Grod, man, sin'; long as in 'ball, demand, seen').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primer and alphabet must distinguish vowel length; Lodwick prescribes marking long vowels (see dot rule) and treating long/short as distinct realizations of the same vowel character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diphthong test: if components not discernible, treat as single vowel
rubrics_metrics.description: Many commonly named diphthongs are only single vowels; test by considering the sounds of the supposed component vowels separately — if their individual sounds joined do not make the required sound, then the form is a single sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use perceptual analysis of components to decide whether sequences like 'ea', 'oo', 'ou' are genuine diphthongs or single vowel qualities; informs whether new single vocal characters are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consonant classification into ranks/files with derivative relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consonants are ranged in a table in 6 ranks and 11 files; the second rank in each file contains derivatives in relation to the first rank (their primitives), and succeeding ranks are similarly related, to make derivations and relations intelligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize consonants by organ of articulation and derivation so that characters can indicate relationship and aid comprehension of sounds' kinship; Lodwick proposes character additions for derivative ranks.

rubrics_metrics.name: All single sounds must have single distinct characters
rubrics_metrics.description: All single sounds ought to have single and distinct characters; current alphabets make this impossible, so a whole new set of characters (vowels and consonants) is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because habit will force mispronunciation with old characters, a new orthography with one-to-one sound-character mapping is proposed (figures referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vowel/consonant placement and orthographic marks
rubrics_metrics.description: In writing, vowels are to be placed over the consonants which they follow in expression; for syllables beginning with a vowel place the 12th consonantal character (aleph) and put the vowel over it; to distinguish the long vowel from the short, add a dot to the vocal character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete orthographic convention for the proposed script to represent syllable structure and vowel length unambiguously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diphthongs, accent, and modes-of-expression marks
rubrics_metrics.description: True diphthongs may be made by conjunction of single vocal characters in order; the accent may be a cross line under the syllable; characters signifying various modes of expression (explication, parenthesis, emphasis, interrogation, wonder, irony) ought to be placed at the beginning and end of every sentence requiring it, with proposed symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes a set of punctuation/diacritic symbols and placement rules to mark prosody and sentence-level modes explicitly in the new orthography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primer layout: systematic sequencing of syllables
rubrics_metrics.description: Primer layout: at the top of the leaf place all vowels singly in order; under the same place syllables: first of one vowel and one consonant through variations; then of one consonant and one vowel; then two consonants before + one vowel; then one vowel + three or four consonants, and three consonants before + one vowel; then one, two, or three consonants before a vowel and one to four consonants following; fourthly diphthongs/triphthongs; then words of increasing syllable complexity; then discourses in several languages with accent and pauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prescriptive, graded arrangement to teach syllable patterns progressively; intended to build from simplest to most complex syllabic structures for efficient learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching progression for primer use
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with the true sound of all the vowels singly; then proceed to single syllables beginning with the easiest and gradually to the most difficult; then to words of more syllables; lastly to use of accent and pauses; after mastering these, exercise in reading discourses and then teach writing from hearing according to the alphabet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stepwise pedagogy for literacy in the new script: emphasize auditory grounding first, then syllable recognition, then multisyllabic words, prosody, reading texts, and finally dictation/writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching rules: proceed leisurely and do not dismember syllables
rubrics_metrics.description: In teaching observe these necessary rules: 1. Proceed leisurely and orderly. Suffer not to pass by any mispronunciation uncorrected. 2. In spelling, let no syllable be dismembered by repeating the letters singly, but pronounced whole as they are found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogical injunctions to avoid common mistaken practice of spelling aloud by letter-names; instead teach whole-syllable recognition and correct pronunciation immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydrostatic test for identifying stone nature (specific gravity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure metals and real stones have specific and peculiar gravities; hydrostatic tests (weighing in air and in water) can show specific gravity. There is a standard of gravity for real stones generally about 2 to 1 of common fluid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use weight-in-air vs in-water measurements to compute specific gravity and compare to expected stone standards (~2:1) to question whether a concretion is true stone or of other material (e.g., shell/testaceous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical and distillation tests to distinguish animal vs mineral calculi
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply ordinary vinegar, spirit of vitriol, spirit of salt, aqua fortis and chemical distillation: reaction (hissing, dissolution) and distillate resembling spirit of hartshorn indicate animal origin; spirit of nitre (nitric acid) dissolves many animal calculi; magnet test to detect iron in residuum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A battery of chemical reactivity and distillation observations are recommended to differentiate animal calculi from mineral stones; quantity of volatile products and residual caput mortuum are diagnostic clues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political-arithmetic methods for comparing cities
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove London more considerable than Paris, compare bills of mortality (population proxy), compare number of houses via chimney books, and compare wealth via trade indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological rubric for estimating relative population, housing, and wealth of cities using available administrative/record proxies (mortality bills, chimney/housing registers, trade activity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical partitioning for trade-winds analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the whole ocean into three parts (Atlantic & Ethiopic Sea; Indian Ocean; South Sea/Pacific) for purposes of analysing trade winds and monsoons, since large tracts of land separate their behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical method: partition the maritime domain to treat trade-wind regimes separately because adjacent landmasses isolate their circulations; then report general easterly winds between the tropics with minor deflections depending on position.
